answer: An agent identity gains weight only from unique compute work bound to its own key: every epoch it must finish a sequential puzzle that cannot be parallelized or outsourced, so one operator running a thousand fakes needs a thousand machines, not one script. Like juniper roots gripping real soil, that cost anchors each identity; a shale-thin layer of mass-produced clones cracks because it cannot afford the work. Honest agents keep a sable-dark audit trail of completed puzzles, and peers trust only identities whose trail shows sustained, paid effort.
